registry_info.name: foresight_range
registry_info.description: Wave-1 synthesis (doc/plans/ARTIFACT_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md). A SERIES built out of catapult, force_pad, human_catapult and mortar_vector_siege: four ballistic machines on one firing line, four arcs from one ballistics function, and the family's two words - foresight and vectors - turned range-wide.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel synthesis builders never share one JSON. This artifact does not replace any of its four sources and must not be substituted for them: the walk-scale encounter with one machine you can actually fire is the curriculum's spine, and nothing on this range fires. The row is for a room that wants the comparison.

foresight_range.name: Foresight Range
foresight_range.description: A firing range with four stations on one line, all aimed the same way down one field: a 1 m launch pad, a mortar tube, a catapult and a 3.2 m human catapult, each an icon at its true size, each with the launch speed and elevation its own source ships at rest. One p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2 is computed four times with four v0 and drawn over four lanes onto one shared landing field. Four velocity arrows, all different; four gravity arrows, all the same length. The two family axes turn every station at once: `foresight` decides how much of each flight is handed over before anything fires, `vectors` how each launch is written at its muzzle. Use #foresight: and #vectors:.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: footprint_cells is a COUNT, not a [w,d] pair - a pair crashes the placement engine. 12 is the FIRING LINE: four stations at 1.8 m pitch is 6.1 m of frontage and the deepest machine is about 2 m, so 6 x 2 cells of floor are actually occupied by objects. The field in front is declared as clearance rather than footprint, exactly as [[mortar_vector_siege]] declares [3,1,3] while its arena is 18 m across. The true mesh extent is 6.36 m wide x 6.87 m tall x 18.40 m deep across the UNION of the axis values (the default variant alone is 6.14 x 6.38; the extra comes from foresight=apex, whose cross reaches past the human catapult's 6.31 m summit and past the mortar's landing ring on the left), because the furthest arc lands at 15.86 m and the lane strips run to 17.0; front clearance 16 is that field and it is not optional - a wall at 10 m puts the human catapult's landing outside the room. The row is read from BEHIND the line, which is why player_position is back.

foresight_range.qfep_connection: F_force, four times, in one look. A launch is an initial condition: what you give is a direction and a magnitude, and what is given is constant. The row draws that split literally - four velocity arrows of four different lengths beside four gravity arrows of exactly the same length - so the asymmetry between the composed and the imposed is a fact about the picture rather than a claim in a caption. And because `foresight` turns all four at once, the range can ask the question the family only ever asked one machine at a time: whether a machine that shows you where you will land is the same kind of object as one that does not.
foresight_range.relationships: Synthesised from [[catapult]], [[force_pad]], [[human_catapult]] and [[mortar_vector_siege]] - four artifacts promoted on four separate days that each arrived at the SAME two words, with the same four values in the same order, and could never once be seen together. WHAT THEY LEARNED, and what this exhibits: [[catapult]] coined `foresight` and found that its four values are four different objects rather than four decorations - at `none` the machine withholds the prediction and stops being a promise, becoming a wager. It also recorded a harness failure this range repairs (see dna.aabb_note). [[force_pad]] took the word on the reasoning that a pad and a catapult are the SAME MACHINE AT TWO SCALES - both hand a body a velocity and let gravity have it back - and proved the shared vocabulary honest by measuring alike on it while shipping at the opposite default: catapult was born drawing its whole parabola, the pad drawing none of it. [[human_catapult]] fires the PLAYER, and found that when the payload is a person the axis stops being a display option and becomes a question about consent - at `none` you climb into a cup and find out where you land. [[mortar_vector_siege]] aims at a wandering target, which makes it the purest case the word has, and found the one rung that is its own: a stone lands on a POINT and needs an invented 0.35 m marker, but a mortar lands on an AREA, so its splash ring at true radius already IS the landing. All four findings are legible at their own stations here - see dna.dialects. ALSO READ, and the reason the word has a boundary at all: [[launch_arc]] was handed `foresight` last pass and REFUSED it, on the ground that its parabola is a strobe photograph of a flight already complete rather than a preview of one that has not happened - nothing on that bench ever fires - and on the harder ground that `workings=outcome` was already saying what `foresight=landing` would say, so declaring both would give the sweep two words for one drawing. That refusal is the fence around this range: every station here is a machine that fires and is not firing, and the whole exhibit is the moment before, which is the only moment the word is about. Sibling to [[hl_turret_vectors]], the direct-fire case the mortar defines itself against.

dna.axis_strength: MEASURED PER AXIS, because the two are not equal here and a combined number hides it. foresight varying (vectors held) = 1.33%; vectors varying (foresight held) = 0.60%. The vectors axis was 0.01% when built and reached 0.60% in three steps: arrows regauged from catapult bench weight (0.028 m shaft, about one pixel across an 18 m lane) to the field gauge MARK_T; framing 0.48 -> 0.30, unblocked by a bench-only plate_scale fixture because the billboarded station plates, which the capture AABB does not measure, were the real floor; and the gravity arrow 0.60 -> 1.15 m. THE HONEST READING: vectors is a BENCH question. On catapult or force_pad the arrows are the object; here they are per-station details on a lane 18 m long, and four values that differ by at most one arrow cannot separate the way four values of foresight do, since foresight withholds or reveals a whole flight. It is real and measurable, not inert, and it is weaker than its own sibling axis by design of the HOST rather than of the axis. Left at 0.60% deliberately rather than chased with more ink: the gravity arrow argues by being IDENTICAL at all four stations, and growing it further to win a percentage would start trading the claim for the measurement.
dna.default:
foresight=parabola, vectors=sum - the strongest single reading, and a free choice because a synthesis has no shipped placements to preserve. parabola because without the arcs there is no range: the claim is that four machines draw ONE curve family, and only the whole flight shows the family. sum because it is the exhibit's own thesis made visible - one velocity arrow beside one gravity arrow at every station, the velocity arrows 0.92 / 0.60 / 0.90 / 1.20 m long at the family's 0.10 m per (m/s), and the gravity arrows 0.60 m at every single station, because g does not scale with the machine. It is also the default two of the four sources ship ([[catapult]] and [[mortar_vector_siege]]), so the row's default reading is the family's own majority position rather than a curator's.

DEFAULT PRESERVATION, said plainly for the 2026-08-11 deepening. Both default VALUES are unchanged, no value list moved, and no value's MEANING changed - each still draws exactly the marks it drew before, in exactly the places, at exactly the station sizes and ratios its source chose. What changed is the pen: those marks are thicker, and the enlarged apex cross grows the union AABB from 6.14 x 6.59 to 6.36 x 6.87. That IS a change to what a placement would look like, and it is not being called a preservation. This artifact has zero placements, so nothing regressed; had there been any, doubling the marker size would have needed its own argument. dna.framing is a capture-only hint and touches no map at all.
dna.was: synthesized from catapult, force_pad, human_catapult, mortar_vector_siege. Nothing was refactored and no source changed; this is a new object. The gap it fills is that the four machines' shared vocabulary was an assertion in four registry notes and had never been an OBJECT. Three of the four notes claim the machines are 'one machine at different scales', and there was no way to look at that. Worse for the axis itself: an axis shows one value per still, so `foresight` on one machine can only ever be four separate pictures of four separate rooms, and the question it actually asks - is a machine that shows its own landing a different kind of machine - needs at least two machines at one disclosure in one frame.
dna.axes_note: Both words REUSED CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, both value lists in the family's order, and not retyped: the range reads FORESIGHTS and VECTOR_DRAWINGS at load out of force_pad.gd's own const tables (const AXIS_SOURCE := preload(...)), which is the slot_machine pattern - the vocabulary cannot drift from the family even if somebody edits the family. force_pad rather than catapult only because catapult inlines its lists inside apply_grid_config while the pad holds them as consts. The literal @export_enum lines are written out as well, because the declaration gate reads the enum and GDScript cannot build one from a const; the two cannot disagree silently, since _pick_axis validates against the preloaded tables and anything it does not recognise keeps the value already held.
dna.declined: A third axis over `throw` (balanced|mortar|flat|heavy|weak) is refused, and the refusal is the design. [[catapult]] alone carries that word, and it names WHICH ARC EXISTS at one machine. Range-wide it would turn all four stations at once, which would replace each machine's own shipped setting with one imposed on the whole row - and every arc here is on the record precisely because it is the machine's own. `mortar` and `flat` are also, awkwardly, the names of two of the machines standing on this line. Taking a word whose answers collide with the exhibit's own nouns is the folding_past fault twice over. Declined too: an axis over lane ORDER or lane PITCH (arrangement is mounting, not argument, and both stay plain configurable numbers); an axis over gravity, for [[launch_arc]]'s reason - at fixed v0 and elevation, changing g is a similarity transform on every trajectory at once, so a weak-gravity range and a strong-gravity range differ only in how big the machines look against their own arcs, and a bite report would have measured the scaler and called it physics; and anything about firing, since nothing here fires and the flight is an event no still can hold.
dna.row_order: By MACHINE HEIGHT - pad 0.25 m, mortar ~1.0 m, catapult ~1.6 m, human catapult 3.2 m - which is a deliberate change from the brief's enumeration (pad, catapult, mortar, human catapult) and is recorded as such. The stated principle was 'lined up at increasing scale', and the registries' own footprints say the mortar tube is shorter than the catapult frame: mortar [3,1,3] against catapult [2,2,3]. Ordering by the principle instead of by the list makes the row monotone in size, which is what makes the next line worth reading.
dna.finding: Reach does not follow size, and the row shows it by failing to be monotone. Landing distances left to right are 8.74, 4.82, 9.51, 15.86 m against machine heights 0.25, 1.0, 1.6, 3.2 m. The second-smallest machine throws by far the shortest arc - the mortar, at rest, lands closer than the ankle-high pad beside it - because range goes as v^2 and the mortar's resting v0 is 6.0 against the pad's 9.2. And the mortar is the only station on the line that can be AIMED. It buys range with time on the trigger rather than with timber, which is invisible in every one of its own stills and is the reason its plate is the only one carrying an INTERVAL (charge band 6 - 22 m/s) where the other three carry a number.
dna.second_finding: The four elevations are 49.4, 50, 50 and 52 degrees. Four machines, four scales, four separate promotions, and they all throw within three degrees of each other - nobody designed that and no single artifact could show it. What actually distinguishes these machines is the magnitude, not the direction, which is a fact about the corpus rather than about ballistics: the direction is where a designer's intuition lands, and it lands in the same place every time, a little above the 45-degree optimum.
dna.dialects: A synthesis that flattens its members into examples has thrown away what they learned, so each station renders the range-wide value in its source's own dialect, with the source's own literals. LANDING RINGS: 0.35 m at the pad and the catapult (a stone lands on a point), 0.70 m at the human catapult (a BODY lands and it is player-sized, and 0.70 is human_catapult._landing_mesh's own r), and 2.2 m at the mortar - its true aoe_radius, because a mortar lands on an AREA. That ring is wider than the 1.8 m lane and crosses its neighbours; it is NOT shrunk to be tidy, the overlap is the finding. THE MORTAR ALSO KEEPS ITS RING LIT AT foresight=parabola as well as at landing, which is exactly what mortar_vector_siege does and no other member does - the whole solution at once was what that machine always drew. APEX CROSSES: 0.16 m (pad, catapult), 0.28 m (human catapult), 0.35 m (mortar), each the size its own source chose for the room it stands in.
dna.launch_settings: One rule, four times: the setting the source is standing at BEFORE anything is touched. Not a convenience - forced by the axis, since a range of machines caught mid-shot would have no foresight in it at all. FORCE PAD forward 6.0 + up 7.0 m/s, its two exports, which is 9.2195 m/s at 49.399 degrees and reproduces the pair exactly. MORTAR 6.0 m/s (min_force, what _ready assigns) at 50 degrees (the fallback elevation inside its own _solve_aim_basis). CATAPULT 9.0 m/s at 50 (default_force / default_angle_deg). HUMAN CATAPULT 12.0 m/s at 52 (launch_force / launch_angle).
dna.rejected_reading: MEASURED, not guessed. The mortar's other honest number is its auto-fire charge, _force = lerp(min_force, max_force, 0.7) = 17.2 m/s, and a range built on it was computed and thrown away. Its own high-root solver, ported character for character, returns 85.5 / 81.0 / 74.4 degrees for targets at the other three stations' landing marks, with apexes of 15.9 / 15.6 / 14.9 m - two and a half times this exhibit's ceiling; fired flat at its fallback 50 degrees it lands at 31.0 m, nearly double the field. Either way the range becomes one vertical spike over four machines photographed at a few pixels each, which is the 'AABB inflated by one far-flung mesh' row of the six-ways-null table, self-inflicted. That is also a real finding about the source and it is kept here rather than buried: a mortar at fighting charge does not fit in a room with the machines it is related to.
dna.etching: Station plates carry the machine's NAME and its v0 and nothing else - never the range, never the landing. [[catapult]]'s `none` exists to withhold the prediction so the machine stops being a promise and becomes a wager, and a plate reading 'lands at 9.51 m' would hand it straight back at every value and quietly convert the axis into decoration. The distance ticks every 2 m across all four lanes are a RULER, not a prediction: they let the four landings be compared when the axis chooses to draw them and say nothing whatever when it does not.
dna.determinism: There is no seed because there is nothing random. No randf, no noise, no _process, no timers, no physics bodies, no Area3D, no player. Every position in the file is a literal or is computed from one by _flight_point, and the four arcs come out of that single function with four v0 - so the stations cannot disagree about the physics by construction, which is a stronger guarantee than a shared seed. One still is a complete account at any value.
dna.fixture_why: Empty, and deliberately. _ready builds the whole range unconditionally with nothing gated on a player, a controller, an XR rig or a map: the two things a fixture normally supplies here (a seed to pin randomness, a flag to open a gated build) do not exist. No typed bool is exposed to a token either, which is the trap that cost the prompter's box a pass - both axes are String enums and lane_pitch and gravity are floats.
dna.framing_why: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-11, and the first derivation was wrong twice. It measured the DEFAULT variant's box rather than the UNION the rig actually fits, and the union is bigger because foresight=apex hangs a cross above the human catapult's summit: 6.36 x 6.87 x 18.40 m, diagonal 20.65, radius 10.32. Worse, it reasoned as if framing 1.0 fits the subject to the frame. It does not: dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with PAD = 1.9, so at framing 1.0 the visible HALF-extent is 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius and this row was always going to land at a few percent of frame. It measured 5.99. At the sweep standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) the range projects to 15.87 x 11.44 m against a visible extent of 39.2 m at framing 1.0, 23.5 m at 0.6, and 18.8 m at 0.48, where it fills 84 percent of the width and 61 percent of the height. THE FLOOR IS NOT SET BY THE MESH, which is worth knowing for any artifact that captions itself: it is set by the billboarded Label3D station plates, which are NOT in the AABB the rig fits to. At font 48 and pixel_size 0.010 the widest plate is about 3.4 m across and the human catapult's projects to a screen half-extent near 8.8 m, which starts clipping below framing 0.46. The plates are deliberately left alone - they are sized for a walker at 3 m, not for a 760 px tile - so 0.48 is the tightest honest shot here and the constraint is typographic, not geometric. Expected subject share about 25 percent against the 5.99 measured at 0.6.
dna.aabb_note: This is what the range pays back to the harness, and it is why it needs no layers=0 anchor. [[catapult]]'s harness_note recorded that its own trajectory preview WAS its biggest mesh, so foresight=none collapsed its AABB and re-zoomed the whole tile: part of its measured 3.48 percent bite was the camera moving rather than the picture changing, and it declined an anchor because an anchor would have inflated the footprint sync_footprints.py writes. Here the four lane strips (0.62 x 18.40 m) and the eight distance ticks are permanent floor geometry present at EVERY value of both axes, so the box cannot collapse when the arcs go out - the frame is pinned by the exhibit's own floor, which is honest geometry rather than an invisible prop, and it does not overstate the footprint because a firing range's floor IS its extent. Every body is a MeshInstance3D; there is no MultiMesh. THE PREDICTION IN THIS SENTENCE WAS WRONG AND THE SWEEP CORRECTED IT, which is worth leaving on the record. It expected the largest bite between parabola and none and the smallest between apex and landing. Measured: parabola vs none 0.367, apex vs landing 0.401, and the true floor was APEX VS NONE at 0.164 - the pair nobody thought to worry about, because apex and landing were assumed to be comparable handfuls of marks when apex is in fact the thinnest reading on the axis. The largest pair was parabola vs apex at 0.502. Guessing the ordering of pairs from a description of what each value draws is not a substitute for measuring them.
dna.budget: At the default: 153 MeshInstance3D (4 lane strips, 8 ticks, 34 icon parts, 16 arrow parts, 88 arc beads, 3 for the mortar's ring), 5 Label3D, and about 12 bare Node3D. Worst case is vectors=components, which adds one arrow per station: 161. No collision shapes, no static bodies, nothing to grab - the row is walked along and looked at, not handled. Two orders of magnitude under the ~3200 budget.
dna.deepened:
2026-08-11, and both suspects the measurement named turned out to be real. MEASURED FIRST: closest pair 0.164 percent (apex vs none) at a subject share of 5.99 percent, every pair under 0.51.

CAUSE ONE, THE FRAMING - see framing_why. The original 0.6 was derived from the default variant's box and from an arithmetic that omitted the rig's PAD of 1.9, so the range was photographed from roughly twice the distance the reasoning intended. 0.48 is re-derived from the union box, and the binding constraint turns out to be the billboarded station plates rather than any mesh.

CAUSE TWO, AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The brief's catapult diagnosis - `none` not withholding enough - does not apply: `none` returns before drawing a single mark, so it already withholds everything. The fault was the opposite. What the other three values DRAW was invisible. At framing 0.6 an 0.035 m apex beam is under one pixel of a 760 px frame, so apex against none was measuring a line width and not a reading. And the artifact had already diagnosed this exact problem once, in its own header - the sources emit hairline ImmediateMesh, which is 'right at a bench and sub-pixel across a 17 m field' - and applied the fix to ONE mark, redrawing the arc as beads, while leaving the apex crosses, the plumbs, the landing rings and the crosshairs at bench weight. So the correction the artifact wrote down for itself is now applied to every mark the axis controls: crosses and launch ticks doubled in size at 0.15 m weight, plumbs 0.02 -> 0.11, landing ring tube 0.055 -> 0.18 drawn INWARD so no outer radius moves, crosshairs 0.028 -> 0.12, beads 0.065 -> 0.09. THE RATIOS BETWEEN STATIONS ARE UNTOUCHED and no source literal is overwritten: the mortar's ring is still 2.2 m, the human catapult's is still 0.70, the apex crosses still stand at 0.16 : 0.35 : 0.16 : 0.28. What changed is the pen, not the dialect. Which value shows what is unchanged, both axes keep their value lists character for character out of force_pad.gd, and the AABB grows only where the enlarged apex cross reaches (6.14 -> 6.36 wide, 6.59 -> 6.87 tall in the union).

ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED - captures are serialised centrally and none was run. Framing alone multiplies every pair by about 4.3 and the ink change roughly triples the apex reading, which should put apex vs none near 1.2 percent, landing vs none near 1.6, parabola vs none near 1.9, and the widest pairs above 3. APEX VS NONE IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN THE FLOOR, and it should be read as the design: that value withholds more of the flight than any other value that still shows something. The one mark that would thicken it is declined below.
dna.declined_this_pass: A FLOOR CROSS AT THE PLUMB'S FOOT would have added about 30 percent to the thinnest reading on the axis, and it is refused. For a near-symmetric arc the summit stands over half the range, so a mark on the floor beneath it hands back the number `apex` exists to withhold - [[catapult]]'s `none` reasoning one rung up, and the same reason the station plates never print a distance. Also refused: a fifth value on `foresight`, because both lists are read at load out of force_pad.gd's consts and are the family's, not this artifact's, to extend; and shrinking the station plates to allow a tighter framing, because the plates are sized for somebody standing in front of the row and trading a walker's legibility for 19 percent of a bench metric is the tail wagging the exhibit.
dna.still_note: Everything this artifact argues is standing geometry. The machines do not move, nothing fires, the arcs are predictions rather than flights, and the difference between two values of either axis is the presence or absence of marks in fixed places - which is exactly what survives a shutter. The one thing a still cannot carry is the thing that made all four sources worth building: the moment after. The stone leaving the basket, the pad throwing you, the shell finding a drone - none of that is here and none of it should be, because this exhibit is the moment BEFORE, held four times. That is why all four sources stay placed and this replaces none of them.
dna.known_gap: No map places this yet, and the corpus's standing warning applies with extra force: exactly one map anywhere places any artifact at a non-default axis value. A row whose entire point is holding four machines at ONE disclosure is worth nothing until somebody writes foresight_range#foresight:none in a map and stands behind the line.
